title: Computer Networking: Original Mock, Streamlined
description: The supplied CCCU mock with repeated questions removed: 65 retained original questions, in their original order. Original stems and visible multiple-choice options are preserved. 64 questions are scored; original Q32 is retained as an unscored discussion because its wording is ambiguous.

scoring.rule: One point per fully correct scored question; no partial or negative marks. 64 available marks across 65 retained questions. Original Q32 is review-only. Equivalent defensible answers are accepted where the source wording is broad. These are practice rules, not the original platform marking scheme.

models.name: OSI and TCP/IP models
models.revise: Separate bits, frames, packets and transport data. Practise mapping the four TCP/IP layers to OSI, then explain encapsulation without assuming every protocol fits one rigid box.
models.check: Explain which information a switch, router and receiving application each examine.

transport.name: Transport and communication
transport.revise: Compare TCP and UDP using reliability, ordering, overhead, ports and application requirements. Distinguish flow control from congestion control and encryption from reliable delivery.
transport.check: Choose a transport for a financial file and for replaceable live samples; justify each trade-off.

services.name: Application protocols and ports
services.revise: Build a compact service-to-purpose table for DNS, DHCP, NTP, HTTP(S), SMTP and SSH/SFTP. Keep mail relay separate from mail submission and retrieval.
services.check: Trace how a newly connected laptop obtains settings, resolves a name and opens a secure website.

video.title: Network Protocols: ARP, FTP, SMTP, HTTP, TLS, DNS, DHCP

devices.name: Devices and client/server roles
devices.revise: Choose devices by the function required. Distinguish repeating, bridging, routing, filtering, proxying and balancing, and recognise that one appliance can combine roles.
devices.check: Draw a request path through an access point, router, proxy and load balancer, explaining each role.

lan.name: LANs, topologies and Wi-Fi
lan.revise: Compare topology failure behaviour, Ethernet versus Wi-Fi, shared radio capacity, broadcast domains and VLAN boundaries. Consider both coverage and user density.
lan.check: Explain why adding access points needs a radio/capacity plan and why a VLAN alone is not an access policy.

video.title: The Bus, Star, Ring, Mesh & Tree Network Topologies

diagnostics.name: IP addressing and troubleshooting
diagnostics.revise: Use addressing, gateway, DNS and translation evidence to localise faults. Know what ping, traceroute and packet capture can demonstrate, and where their evidence stops.
diagnostics.check: For a host that reaches an IP address but not a hostname, choose a targeted next test and explain why.

process.name: Network design process
process.revise: Work from measurable requirements through analysis, logical design, physical design, validation and acceptance. Distinguish top-down, bottom-up and hybrid decisions.
process.check: Turn a vague request for a fast network into a measurable acceptance criterion and a relevant test.

campus.name: Campus hierarchy and resilience
campus.revise: Separate access, distribution and core functions. Evaluate redundancy, capacity, failure domains, failover and growth using the whole path rather than a device count.
campus.check: Identify shared power, links or providers that can defeat an apparently redundant design.

threats.name: Threats and vulnerability analysis
threats.revise: Identify the mechanism and affected asset for floods, spoofing, poisoning, hijacking, injection, memory errors and social engineering. Do not label every outage an attack.
threats.check: For each threat, state the evidence that distinguishes it from a configuration error and select one relevant control.

controls.name: Security controls and validation
controls.revise: Distinguish IDS alerts from inline prevention, validate rules, combine controls, protect credentials and traffic, and apply identity-based access decisions.
controls.check: Explain the limits of encryption, segmentation and monitoring individually, then combine them in a small security plan.

ids: NIST intrusion detection and prevention guide

questions.prompt: Match the protocol to its role in delivering content over the internet (as per the lecture):
items: Retrieves web content from servers
Transports user data with reliability
Transports packets across networks
Transports control information and checks for delivery

questions.explanation: The intended teaching matches are Hub, Switch, Router and Bridge. A switch is a multiport bridge, so the MAC-learning description fits both. The final row is broad enough to describe a bridge, switch or router depending on the type of segmentation; these defensible alternatives are accepted. Original option labels ending in Device are retained as shown in the PDF.
questions.objective: Distinguish repeating, bridging, switching and routing fairly.
questions.prompt: Select the correct device-function pairings for common network hardware mentioned in the notes
items: Device that broadcasts incoming traffic to all ports in a LAN
Device that learns MAC addresses and forwards based on them within a LAN
Device used to connect separate networks and perform path selection
Device that segments a LAN and can connect disparate LANs
questions.optionProvenance: All four original visible response labels retained exactly; broad device descriptions accept technically defensible alternatives.
